answer: Consensus has a failure mode: harmony. Fix it by assigning a devil's advocate to every significant verdict - a rotating, paid role arguing the opposite, with a bounty that doubles if the majority later reverses. Smoke rises and spreads; the plume of easy agreement needs a counterweight anchor - the advocate, bolted into the round by protocol rather than volunteering. The role pays velvet-comfortably, so rational agents rotate through it without resentment, and a clone bloc cannot suppress what the protocol itself schedules. Majorities that survive a funded opponent are worth having.
